title: Paul's Defense Before the Jerusalem Crowd

questions.question: Paul described his upbringing in his defense speech. Under whose feet was he educated?
options: Gamaliel
Caiaphas
Hillel
Shammai
questions.explanation: Acts 22:3 (ESV): "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia, but brought up in this city, educated at the feet of Gamaliel according to the strict manner of the law of our fathers..."

questions.question: Paul described himself before his conversion as being zealous for God. What had he done to the followers of the Way?
options: Persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering to prison both men and women
Reported them to the Sanhedrin and instigated their trials
Organized synagogue hearings to expel Christians from worship
Written letters to all the synagogues warning against the Way
questions.correctAnswer: Persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering to prison both men and women
questions.explanation: Acts 22:4 (ESV): "I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering to prison both men and women,"

questions.question: Paul recounted that on the road to Damascus a great light flashed around him and he fell to the ground. The voice called him by name twice and asked: "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?" Paul asked who it was. What was the answer?
options: "I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting."
"I am the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
"I am the one you hate; I am Jesus the Christ."
"I am the risen Christ, Lord of heaven and earth."
questions.correctAnswer: "I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting."
questions.explanation: Acts 22:8 (ESV): "And I answered, 'Who are you, Lord?' And he said to me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting.'"

questions.question: After the Damascus road encounter, Paul was led by the hand into Damascus being blinded. Later Ananias came to visit him. How did Ananias describe himself and his character reference?
options: A devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus
A disciple sent by the Lord himself with a message for Paul
A believer who had witnessed the first Pentecost in Jerusalem
An elder of the Damascus synagogue who had been visited by an angel
questions.correctAnswer: A devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus
questions.explanation: Acts 22:12 (ESV): "And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who lived there,"

questions.question: Ananias told Paul he had been appointed to know God's will and to see the Righteous One and hear his voice. For what purpose was this?
options: To be a witness for him to everyone of what he had seen and heard
To preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ
To plant churches across the Roman Empire to its western boundary
To write letters that would guide believers for all generations
questions.correctAnswer: To be a witness for him to everyone of what he had seen and heard
questions.explanation: Acts 22:15 (ESV): "for you will be a witness for him to everyone of what you have seen and heard."

questions.question: After returning to Jerusalem, Paul had a vision in the temple where the Lord spoke to him. What did the Lord say about Paul's testimony to the people of Jerusalem?
options: "Make haste and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about me."
"Stay in Jerusalem and testify to them boldly for I will protect you."
"Your testimony here is complete; go now to the Gentile nations."
"Do not fear them; my Spirit will give you the words to speak."
questions.correctAnswer: "Make haste and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about me."
questions.explanation: Acts 22:18 (ESV): "and saw him saying to me, 'Make haste and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about me.'"

questions.question: The crowd listened to Paul's speech until he mentioned being sent to the Gentiles. What happened then?
options: They raised their voices saying "Away with such a fellow from the earth! For he should not be allowed to live."
"They called for the high priest to judge him immediately."
"They threw dust in the air and tore off their cloaks, demanding his death."
Both A and C happened together — they cried out and also threw dust/tore cloaks.
questions.correctAnswer: Both A and C happened together — they cried out and also threw dust/tore cloaks.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:22-23 (ESV): "...they raised their voices and said, 'Away with such a fellow from the earth!'... they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and flinging dust into the air,"

questions.question: The tribune ordered Paul to be examined by flogging. What did Paul say that stopped this?
options: "Is it lawful for you to flog a man who is a Roman citizen and uncondemned?"
"I appeal to Caesar; you have no authority over me."
"I am a Roman citizen by birth and demand a proper trial."
"The law of Rome forbids flogging of citizens without trial."
questions.correctAnswer: "Is it lawful for you to flog a man who is a Roman citizen and uncondemned?"
questions.explanation: Acts 22:25 (ESV): "...Paul said to the centurion who was standing by, 'Is it lawful for you to flog a man who is a Roman citizen and uncondemned?'"

questions.question: The tribune told Paul he had bought his Roman citizenship for a large sum. What did Paul say in response?
options: "But I am a citizen by birth."
"And I received it through no less a price."
"The gift of God is worth more than any citizen's rights."
"Then you know the rights it requires you to uphold."
questions.correctAnswer: "But I am a citizen by birth."
questions.explanation: Acts 22:28 (ESV): "The tribune answered, 'I bought this citizenship for a large sum.' Paul said, 'But I am a citizen by birth.'"

questions.question: Why did the tribune release Paul from his bonds and bring him before the chief priests and the council?
options: He wanted to know the real reason the Jews were accusing Paul
He had received orders from the governor to investigate the matter
He feared that Paul would die and he would be blamed
He was hoping the Sanhedrin would formally charge Paul for trial
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to know the real reason the Jews were accusing Paul
questions.explanation: Acts 22:30 (ESV): "But on the next day, desiring to know the real reason why he was being accused by the Jews, he unbound him and commanded the chief priests and all the council to meet..."

questions.question: Paul told the crowd in Jerusalem he had been born in Tarsus. Where had he been brought up?
options: In this city (Jerusalem)
In Antioch of Syria
In Alexandria of Egypt
In Caesarea of Palestine
questions.explanation: Acts 22:3 (ESV): "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia, but brought up in this city,"

questions.question: Paul said he was being sent to the Gentiles. He quoted the Lord saying he was being "sent far away to the..."?
options: Gentiles
nations
ends of the earth
Greek world
questions.explanation: Acts 22:21 (ESV): "And he said to me, 'Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"

questions.question: After the crowd cried out, the tribune brought Paul into the barracks. The soldiers who were about to flog Paul IMMEDIATELY drew back when they heard he was a Roman citizen. Why was even the tribune alarmed?
options: Because he had bound a Roman citizen
Because he had struck Paul in the crowd
Because he had unlawfully arrested Paul
Because he had threatened a Roman senator
questions.correctAnswer: Because he had bound a Roman citizen
questions.explanation: Acts 22:29 (ESV): "...the tribune also was afraid, for he realized that Paul was a Roman citizen and that he had bound him."

questions.question: Ananias told Paul to "rise and be baptized and wash away your sins, calling on..."?
options: his name
the Lord's name
Jesus's name
the name of God
questions.explanation: Acts 22:16 (ESV): "And now why do you wait? Rise and be baptized and wash away your sins, calling on his name."

questions.question: Paul saw the men in the crowd witness his companions leading him, but why could they not understand the voice that spoke to Paul on the Damascus road?
options: They heard the sound but did not understand the voice of the one speaking to him
The voice was inaudible to all but Paul alone
They fell asleep like the disciples at the transfiguration
The voice spoke in a heavenly language unknown to human ears
questions.correctAnswer: They heard the sound but did not understand the voice of the one speaking to him
questions.explanation: Acts 22:9 (ESV): "Now those who were with me saw the light but did not understand the voice of the one who was speaking to me."

key_verse_text: "for you will be a witness for him to everyone of what you have seen and heard."
